title: Drug money and the State pharmacy permit at the same address
question: Do the San Francisco pharmacies and suppliers that Medicaid paid for drugs hold a State Board of Pharmacy permit, and since when?
finding: 40 San Francisco pharmacies and medical-supply companies drew $100,000 or more of Medicaid drug money in 2018-2024. 9 have no Board of Pharmacy permit of any kind at their address in the November 2026 file ($17.1 million). 6 of them are medical-supply companies ($15.2 million, led by SUNRISE MEDICAL SUPPLIES INC ($4.9 million, 2018-2024); SF ROYAL MEDICAL SUPPLY, INC ($4.4 million, 2018-2024)); the file has no licence type for medical-device sellers, so for them the absence shows nothing. The 3 pharmacies without a permit in the file: SAN FRANCISCO STATE UNIVERSITY STUDENT HEALTH SERVICES ($955,250, 2018-2024); WALGREEN CO. ($647,385, 2018-2020); WALGREEN CO ($214,586, 2018-2024). 2 sit at an address whose only permit was issued after their Medicaid drug money ended: ALTO PHARMACY LLC ($1.9 million, 2020-2024); MISSION WELLNESS HEALTHCARE LLC ($923,542, 2018-2023). 1 more holds a permit issued after their drug money began, and 4 Walgreens stores carry the chain's 28 August 2025 permit date (screen 'boards-walgreens-reissue').
how: Every San Francisco billing number with $100,000 or more of Medicaid drug money, 2018-2024, in the federal drug file whose federal registry entry is a pharmacy (taxonomy 3336) or a medical-supply company (332B). Matched to the Board of Pharmacy file first on the State licence number the provider reported to the federal registry, then on street number and name within San Francisco. The permit shown is the retail or hospital pharmacy permit where there is one, otherwise a clinic or wholesaler permit.
limits: The Board file lists only permits that are current or lapsed; a pharmacy that closed, moved or changed owner had its old permit cancelled, and the file then shows only the new one, so a recent issue date is the ordinary mark of a change of owner or address, not of billing without a permit. A medical-supply company that sells only equipment and supplies needs no pharmacy permit; one that sells prescription devices may hold a licence the Board no longer issues in this file. Drug money in the federal file can be billed under one location's number for several stores. Address matching can miss a store whose address is written differently.
